records.disposition: ready-for-root-record within same-owner repaired-QSM-interface use responsibility; no independent fullproof acceptance
clauses: Fix an integer $d\geq1$, the lattice $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, and at each site the two-dimensional complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H_i=\mathbb C^2$ with an orthonormal basis $e_{+1},e_{-1}$. Define the dimensionless local spin matrix $Z_i$ by $Z_i e_s=s e_s$ for $s\in\{-1,+1\}$. It is self-adjoint, diagonal in this basis, and has operator norm one. The local matrix algebras and factor inclusions are those of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]], and the interaction/Hamiltonian convention is that of [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]].

Let $J_{ij}=J_{ji}\in\mathbb R$ be specified for distinct sites, and let $h_i\in\mathbb R$. Assume there is a finite $R\geq0$ such that $J_{ij}=0$ when $\|i-j\|_\infty>R$, and
$$\sup_{i\in\Gamma}\left(|h_i|+\sum_{j\ne i}|J_{ij}|\right)<\infty.$$
The associated quantum interaction in the convention of [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]] is
$$\Phi(\{i\})=-h_iZ_i,\qquad \Phi(\{i,j\})=-J_{ij}Z_iZ_j\quad(i\ne j),\qquad \Phi(S)=0\ \text{for all other finite }S.$$
Its per-site norm sum is finite by the displayed bound, and all its terms are diagonal and commute. For a finite $\Lambda\subset\Gamma$, its free-boundary Hamiltonian is
$$H_\Lambda=-\sum_{i\in\Lambda}h_iZ_i-\sum_{\{i,j\}\subseteq\Lambda}J_{ij}Z_iZ_j,$$
where every unordered pair is counted once.
records.focused_repaired_interface_disposition: Uses actual nonzero finite spin2configuration Hilbert spaces, self-adjoint norm1local Zmatrices and tensor-with-identity inclusions. Finite-range diagonal singleton/pair terms define the stated bounded interaction with each unordered pair counted once. No diagonal-only restriction of the full local matrix algebra or infinite density representation is introduced.

clauses:
Assume Countable Choice and the finite-matrix C*-identity for the local spin algebras. Let $\alpha_t$ be the thermodynamic dynamics for the diagonal interaction of [[def-qsm-diagonal-ising-interaction]], as constructed under the exact hypotheses of [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]]. For a local observable $A\in\mathcal A_X$, define the finite self-adjoint matrix
$$K_X:=\sum_{S:S\cap X\ne\varnothing}\Phi(S),$$
where the sum ranges over the singleton and pair supports of that Ising interaction. Then the sum is finite and
$$\alpha_t(A)=e^{itK_X/\hbar}Ae^{-itK_X/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).$$
In particular, every local diagonal observable is fixed by $\alpha_t$. The formula is exact for this commuting diagonal model and uses the full local matrix algebra; it does not restrict observables to diagonal matrices.

**Given:** Countable Choice, the finite-matrix C*-identity, the finite-range diagonal interaction of [[def-qsm-diagonal-ising-interaction]], its free-boundary finite-volume dynamics, $\hbar>0$, and the thermodynamic limit stated in [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]].

[F1] [[def-qsm-diagonal-ising-interaction]] gives diagonal self-adjoint terms $\Phi(S)$ with finite range and bounded per-site norm sum; each singleton or pair term has finite support.

[F2] [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]] states, under Countable Choice and [A2], that free-boundary finite-volume dynamics converge in norm on local observables, uniformly on compact time intervals, to the exhaustion-independent group $\alpha_t$.

clauses: Assume Countable Choice and the finite-matrix C*-identity for the local spin algebras. Let $\omega$ be a $\beta$-KMS state, with $\beta>0$, for the thermodynamic dynamics of [[def-qsm-diagonal-ising-interaction]] in the full quasi-local matrix algebra. For every finite region $\Lambda$ and any two distinct product-basis configurations $\sigma,\tau\in\{-1,+1\}^\Lambda$, the local matrix unit $E_{\sigma,\tau}$ satisfies $\omega(E_{\sigma,\tau})=0$. Consequently the density matrix representing $\omega$ on each finite local matrix algebra is diagonal in the joint eigenbasis of the matrices $Z_i$.
**Given:** Countable Choice, the finite-matrix C*-identity, the diagonal Ising dynamics, a $\beta$-KMS state for it in the convention of [[def-qsm-kms-state]], and the closed-strip hypotheses below.
